chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, from al-Asamm, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The wretches among your dead are the bachelors (unmarried men).'

key_terms.رُذَالُ: Wretches or lowly ones (plural of radhel)

ai.seo_question: What does the Shia hadith say about the spiritual status of unmarried men after death?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise narration where the Prophet identifies unmarried men as 'ruthal' (wretches or lowly ones) among the dead, emphasizing marriage as a fundamental Sunnah. Shia scholars interpret this not as a strict obligation for all, but as a strong recommendation for those capable, linking the preservation of lineage and spiritual stability to one's posthumous status. This highlights the sociological dimension of marriage in Shia jurisprudence as a means of completing half of one's faith.
